source.title: Model-Behavior Alignment under Flexible Evaluation: When the Best-Fitting Model Isn't the Right One

record.tranche_reason: The study tests flexible model-to-behavior alignment and reports that it can make different models' representational geometries more alike while reducing model identifiability. This refines the interpretation of alignment results, but it does not test native convergence with model scale.
record.gate_note: The study measures representational geometry before and after linear alignment to the same human odd-one-out dataset. It also reports model-recovery and predictive-accuracy results under different data sizes and evaluation flexibilities; those measures concern whether flexible evaluation identifies the data-generating model, not convergence of representations as defined by the claim versions. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a model-recovery study of model-to-human-behavior alignment, asking whether flexible linear probing identifies the data-generating model. It does not measure whether independently trained models' representations converge natively, with scale, across modalities or across seeds. It neither cites nor tests the Platonic Representation Hypothesis or convergent learning. The one between-model result (Fig. S6) compares RDMs after each model is linearly fitted to the same human target, so that convergence is induced by design. The only native figure is a passing description of unaligned off-diagonal RDM correlations, typically 0.2–0.5, with no scale sweep, metric comparison or analysis of causes. This fits fits_no_version rather than a test of V6 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors also attribute misidentification mainly to alignment-induced shifts in representational geometry and to higher post-alignment effective dimensionality. They recommend changing stimuli (OOD or controversial), metrics (constrained readouts) and models, rather than relying on ever-larger flexible fits.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses full-matrix linear probing to align pretrained vision-model representations to human odd-one-out behavior, followed by synthetic model-recovery simulations. It does not reproduce the original sources' tests of scale convergence or convergence across random seeds.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that predictive accuracy rises and model-recovery performance falls as evaluation flexibility increases. Recovery improves with more training triplets but remains below 80% at 4.2 million. The RDM comparison uses whitened Pearson correlation; alternative similarity measures are not tested.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probing of 20 diverse vision models to the same human odd-one-out data drives their RDMs toward a shared geometry, a 'bright band' of high post-alignment similarity. Before alignment, off-diagonal whitened Pearson RDM correlations are typically 0.2–0.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitting flexible linear readouts to a common behavioral target makes diverse models' representational geometries similar. This erodes model identity, so post-hoc linear alignment can manufacture apparent convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Model recovery under full linear probing plateaus below 80% at 4.2M triplets (about 70% with 30 models). Objective-family recovery reaches about 73.7% and architecture-family recovery 70.3%. Misidentification is predicted by alignment-induced geometric shift and by post-alignment effective dimensionality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under flexible linear evaluation, functionally different models become behaviorally near-interchangeable, so predictive accuracy does not identify the generating model or its objective or architecture family.

record.problems: The study is limited to behavioral judgments from the THINGS odd-one-out task and a closed candidate set of vision models; the authors state that results may not generalize to neural data. RDM convergence is reported qualitatively in the text, with exact post-alignment similarities only in a figure. The study does not test scaling of model size or capability, alternative RDM similarity measures, or out-of-distribution inputs.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported per-model RDM similarity values were available in the text; Figure S6 is described only in aggregate. Predictive-accuracy values in Table S1 and parameter-control results in Figure S3 were not included because they do not directly measure convergence between model representations.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep. No native cross-architecture convergence trend.
No language models and no image–caption alignment.
No direct model-to-model representation mapping or stitching. Candidates are fitted to another model's simulated behavioral choices, not its representations.
No features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
No comparison of similarity measures, neighbour settings or out-of-distribution inputs for between-model convergence. Metric flexibility is studied only for model-to-human prediction.
No test of how complete or plateaued native convergence is, or of whether shared data or objectives explain it. Only a one-line descriptive range for unaligned RDM correlations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5 'tests' with limits_scope verdicts on V6 and V7 is not supported. Those verdicts rest on R1, whose convergence is induced by fitting every model to the same target, which the rules exclude. The study's metric-dependence argument concerns model-to-brain and behavior evaluation, not cross-model convergence. The unaligned 0.2–0.5 RDM correlation range is a passing description in a figure caption, not a test of V7's partial-convergence clause.

versions.untested_parts: No scale sweep or measure of whether independently trained models' representations converge as model size or capability increases.
No paired image-caption representation alignment or scaling of vision and language model capability.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations for shared features or subspaces.
The study maps model representations to human judgments, not one model's representations onto another's.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are examined.
The study varies linear-evaluation flexibility and training-set size, but does not compare alternative representational similarity measures, nearest-neighbor settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.

The study tests geometry after post-hoc alignment to a shared behavioral dataset. It does not test native convergence, isolate shared training data or objectives as causes, or establish a plateau in pairwise representational similarity.

rows.subject: all 20 ANN models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared squared-Euclidean RDM geometry before and after full-matrix linear alignment to THINGS odd-one-out judgments.
rows.measure: Between-model similarity of representational dissimilarity matrices
rows.value: After alignment, the figure shows a bright band of high off-diagonal similarity; the text says models' geometries shift toward VICE and that alignment erodes model individuality. Exact post-alignment correlations are not stated.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative result; no per-model or exact post-alignment correlation values are given in the text. The models were separately fitted to the same behavioral target, so this is convergence induced by post-hoc alignment, not evidence of native convergence.
rows.check: The post-alignment similarity comes from separately fitting each model's W to the same THINGS odd-one-out target. That is convergence imposed by the procedure, not models' representations becoming alike. It does not measure V6's metric or input dependence of native convergence, nor V7's causes or plateau. The baseline (unaligned off-diagonal whitened Pearson 0.2–0.5) is the only native value, and it comes from one measure with no comparison condition. The post-alignment value is figure-only.

rows.subject: all 20 ANN models (aggregate model-recovery simulations)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained representations; models fitted to synthetic responses
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of synthetic training triplets used to fit candidate models and measured correct recovery of the data-generating model.
rows.note: Model recovery is not itself a measure of representational convergence, so this result is recorded as bearing on the study's broader concern about interpreting flexible alignment, not as a direct result for a claim version.
rows.check: Model-recovery accuracy is not a convergence measure. The 'partial' state has no version to refer to. The value itself (below 80% at 4.2M triplets) is correctly read.

rows.subject: all 20 ANN models (aggregate model-recovery simulations)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained representations; models fitted to synthetic responses
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of synthetic training triplets used to fit candidate models and measured correct recovery of the data-generating model.
rows.value: Below 20% for datasets with thousands of triplets.
rows.note: The text says recovery improves as dataset size grows. This is model identification performance, not a direct measure of geometric convergence.
rows.check: Model-recovery accuracy (below 20% at thousands of triplets) is not a convergence measure. The state has no version referent.

rows.subject: all 20 ANN models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Compared predictive accuracy and model-recovery accuracy across evaluation-flexibility levels, from zero-shot through diagonal and rectangular transforms to full linear probing.
rows.measure: Trade-off between mean predictive accuracy and model-recovery accuracy
rows.baseline: Zero-shot evaluation and lower-flexibility transformations are the reference conditions.
rows.value: The text reports that greater flexibility increases predictive accuracy at the expense of model discriminability; exact values are figure-only.
rows.note: This compares evaluation performance and identifiability, rather than measuring convergence of representational distances directly.
rows.check: The accuracy–identifiability trade-off concerns model-to-behavior evaluation metrics, not between-model representational convergence. The state has no version referent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
